assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminators on clustered single molecules is a true game-changer: a molecular-chemistry solution (nucleotide design, surface chemistry, fluorescence detection) that collapsed sequencing cost by orders of magnitude and reshaped biology and medicine.
assessment.attribution: The Solexa/Illumina chemistry traces to Balasubramanian and Klenerman; Rothberg (pyrosequencing-based 454 platform) and Mayer (clustering) are parallel contributions. Two or three names fit; I would honour the Cambridge chemistry rather than the commercial platforms.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of universal use and complete independent validation; recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as chemistry rather than medicine/physiology or technology.
Credit split between Cambridge, Rothberg (454) and Mayer (clustering) is contested in part.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics made ab initio dynamics routine, allowing bond breaking, solvation and condensed-phase chemistry to be simulated without empirical force fields. It is foundational for quantitative theory connected to experiment.
assessment.attribution: A single 1985 paper with exactly two originators; attribution is unusually clean and fits a two-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Forty years of use and thousands of derivative applications; the method is stable and widely validated, so recognition is well timed.
uncertainties: Parrinello also appears in other candidates (metadynamics, ML potentials); the committee must avoid an awkward overlap of credit.
Cost and DFT accuracy limits constrain some applications, though this does not undermine the method.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling is simple, general and ubiquitous in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis; a straightforward route to a bond that was previously hard to make, in the spirit of prizes that reward not overcomplicating matters.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general catalytic amination independently and then drove ligand design; Kosugi/Migita's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor but not the general method. Two laureates is a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of industrial use and robust confirmation; the 2010 cross-coupling prize partly overlaps in subject, which may make some colleagues hesitate.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize may be judged as insufficiently new.
Credit for precursor work by Kosugi and Migita.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles enabled clinical delivery of siRNA and mRNA, a decisive real-world consequence, since they made the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines and RNA therapeutics possible. The core is lipid chemistry and self-assembly with well-understood pH-dependent mechanism.
assessment.attribution: The foundational formulation and ionizable-lipid concepts came from Cullis' Vancouver group (Hope, Madden, with MacLachlan); Langer and Anderson contributed polymer/lipid delivery screening. Fair allocation to three is possible but not unambiguous.
assessment.maturity: Clinically proven at global scale; the 2023 Medicine prize recognised mRNA modification, leaving the delivery side open. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Individual credit within the Vancouver group and relative to Langer/Anderson and to Acuitas/Moderna lipid designers.
Chemistry versus medicine boundary after the 2023 Medicine prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned interatomic potentials deliver near-quantum accuracy at force-field cost and are changing how reaction and materials simulations are done. As a simulation scientist I see this as a real shift, though not yet as settled as classical methods.
assessment.attribution: Behler-Parrinello neural-network potentials (2007) and Csányi/Bartók Gaussian approximation potentials are the two founding lines; Parrinello's overlap with Car-Parrinello complicates a combined configuration. Behler and Csányi would be the cleanest pair.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing with broad adoption, but transferability, long-range physics and data requirements are still active issues; slightly early relative to the leading candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the field has stabilised enough, versus foundation models now emerging.
Dependence of credit on Parrinello's other candidacy and on newer equivariant architectures.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mass-spectrometry-based quantitative proteomics turned protein identification into a systematic, proteome-wide measurement, a lasting change to molecular biology and a natural follow-on to the 2002 Fenn/Tanaka prize.
assessment.attribution: Mann (high-resolution, SILAC, proteome-scale workflows), Aebersold (ICAT, SRM/SWATH) and Yates (shotgun/MudPIT, database search) are the principal figures; Hunt, Gygi and Heck are also strong, so cutting to three is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Mature and universally used; recognition is fully timely, and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Choosing three among at least six strong contributors.
Overlap with other mass-spectrometry candidates (Orbitrap, native MS).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another without double-strand breaks, enabling precise genome chemistry with therapeutic consequences; it is a clear example of chemical thinking (deaminase engineering) creating a new capability.
assessment.attribution: David Liu is the clear originator of cytosine and adenine base editors, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead trainees; Kondo and Nishida's Target-AID is a parallel contribution. A one-person prize is possible; Liu also appears in prime editing and DNA-encoded libraries.
assessment.maturity: First clinical base-editing treatments and many trials are underway, but the full therapeutic track record is still being built; this is somewhat early compared with the others.
uncertainties: Following the 2020 CRISPR prize, the committee may consider genome editing already recognised.
Priority between Liu and the Kondo/Nishida group; long-term clinical safety evidence is limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues is a new pharmacological paradigm that makes formerly undruggable proteins accessible; the chemistry is conceptually simple and the consequences are already visible in clinical programmes.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched PROTAC (Sakamoto 2001), while Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and degrader design were decisive for usable molecules; Handa/Ito's thalidomide-cereblon discovery underpins molecular glues. Three can be named, but it leaves out important parts.
assessment.maturity: Many compounds are in phase 2-3 trials with approvals still pending, so recognition could be somewhat premature; the concept itself is well confirmed.
uncertainties: Clinical proof of value is incomplete.
Allocation among PROTAC originators, VHL/cereblon ligand developers and the thalidomide mechanism discoverers.
